title: SHEGLAM’s New Blush Drops Put Dewy Colour in the Spotlight
excerpt: SHEGLAM has introduced two blush formulas focused on fresh colour and a dewy finish. Here is what the new textures offer and how to wear them.
body:
SHEGLAM is adding two playful formats to its cheek-colour range: Bubble Dew Blush Serum and Squeeze & Dot Shimmer Blush Paint. The launch reflects continued interest in fresh-looking colour, lightweight textures and makeup that can be applied in small, buildable amounts.

Two formulas, two finishes

According to Dubai Beauty Spot’s launch coverage, Bubble Dew Blush Serum comes in six shades, while Squeeze & Dot Shimmer Blush Paint is available in four. The names point to two different approaches: a serum-style blush for a fresh wash of colour and a shimmer format for a more light-catching finish. Check SHEGLAM’s official product pages for the current shade names, ingredient lists and availability before buying.

How to apply dewy blush

Start with a small amount on the cheek and blend upwards towards the temples. Liquid and serum textures can be pigmented, so build the colour in thin layers rather than applying too much at once. If you are layering blush over foundation, gently tap the product into place to avoid disturbing the base underneath.

Choose the finish that suits your routine

A dewy finish can complement a fresh, skin-like makeup look, while shimmer adds visible reflection. If your skin tends to become shiny during the day, you can keep the glow concentrated on the cheeks and lightly set other areas. Those who prefer a softer finish may want to test the product in natural light before adding more.

As with any new makeup launch, shade appearance can vary with skin tone, lighting and the products underneath. Review the official details and patch-test if you know you are sensitive to cosmetic ingredients.

Source: Dubai Beauty Spot, “SHEGLAM’s Latest Blush Drops Are Here to Dew It and Dot It.”

title: ALASTIN Updates Its Eye Complex with TriHex+
excerpt: ALASTIN has announced an updated Restorative Eye Complex featuring TriHex+ technology. Here are the reported formula details and what shoppers should know.
body:
ALASTIN Skincare has announced an updated Restorative Eye Complex featuring its TriHex+ technology. The launch is part of the wider eye-care category, where brands often focus on the appearance of fine lines, puffiness and skin texture around the eyes. The product announcement is a useful reminder to distinguish a formula’s stated ingredients from the results a shopper can expect.

What the updated formula highlights

In its 26 October 2026 announcement, parent company Galderma highlights TriHex+ alongside Octapeptide-45, Acetyl Tetrapeptide-2 and a dill and blackberry blend. For the exact ingredient list, directions and any cautions, refer to the product packaging and official ALASTIN product information. Ingredient names alone do not establish how well a product will work for an individual.

What the brand-reported evaluation says

Galderma reports an evaluation involving 29 participants and describes improvements by week 12 in the appearance of crow’s feet, under-eye puffiness and upper-eyelid fine lines. These are company-reported findings, not a guarantee of results for every user. When assessing a cosmetic study, it is useful to look at the study design, the measures used, the size of the group and whether the findings have been independently replicated.

How to choose an eye product

Consider your main concern, the product’s texture and whether it fits comfortably into your existing routine. Apply eye products only as directed and avoid getting them into the eyes. If you have persistent irritation, an eye condition or use prescription skincare, ask a qualified healthcare professional whether the formula is appropriate for you.

The updated product was announced for the United States market. Availability and launch timing may differ in the UAE and other regions, so check official local channels before looking for it in store.

Source: Galderma, “Galderma Launches ALASTIN Restorative Eye Complex with TriHex+,” 26 October 2026.

title: At-Home Beauty Devices: What to Know About TAFITIE’s Ultrasound Launch
excerpt: TAFITIE has introduced a 10 MHz at-home ultrasound beauty device. We look at the announced features and the questions to ask before trying home technology.
body:
At-home beauty technology continues to offer consumers new ways to structure a skincare routine. One recent product announcement is TAFITIE’s 10 MHz ultrasound beauty device, positioned for home use. As with any device that uses energy-based technology, it is important to understand the manufacturer’s intended use and instructions rather than assuming that a technical specification guarantees a particular result.

Features announced by the manufacturer

According to the launch release published through Newsfile, the device has two titanium heads, four named modes (INFUSE, GLOW, LIFT and CLEAR) and a dedicated coupling gel. The release listed a price of US$1,599.99 and availability in the United States and Canada. These are manufacturer-provided details and may change; check the current official listing for updated pricing, compatibility and regional availability.

What to check before purchasing

  • Read the intended-use statement and full user manual.
  • Check contraindications, including whether the device is suitable for your health circumstances and skin condition.
  • Confirm which coupling product is required and how the device and heads should be cleaned.
  • Understand the return policy, warranty and availability of customer support.

Do the mode names prove results?

No. Terms such as “lift” or “glow” describe how a product is marketed, not independent proof of a specific outcome. The Beauty Briefing’s coverage of the launch also provides context for treating the device’s claims cautiously. Home-use devices should not automatically be assumed to deliver the same outcomes as professional treatments.

Follow the instructions exactly and stop use if you experience discomfort or an unexpected skin reaction. If you have a skin condition or are unsure whether ultrasound technology is appropriate for you, seek advice from a qualified healthcare professional before use.

Sources: TAFITIE launch release via Newsfile and The Beauty Briefing.

title: Beauty’s Latest Launches Blend Skincare, Makeup and Playful Design
excerpt: From serum-style blush to skincare-led formulas, new beauty products are mixing texture, colour and design. Here is how to separate novelty from usefulness.
body:
New beauty products are increasingly presented as an experience as well as a formula: texture, packaging, shade names and application methods all play a part in how a launch is introduced. The strongest product for your routine, however, is not necessarily the one with the most eye-catching packaging. It is the one that suits your preferences, works with the products you already use and earns a regular place in your makeup bag.

Texture is part of the story

One example is the latest SHEGLAM blush launch, covered by Dubai Beauty Spot, which includes a serum-style blush and a shimmer paint format. These formats offer different finishes and application experiences, showing how brands use texture to distinguish products within a familiar category.

Skincare-inspired does not mean one-size-fits-all

Makeup products may highlight a lightweight feel, a serum-like consistency or ingredients associated with skincare. Those details can be useful, but they should not replace checking the full ingredient list, directions and suitability for your skin. A product marketed as hydrating, for example, may still feel different depending on your skin type and the other layers underneath it.

Build a considered beauty edit

Before buying a launch, ask three simple questions: Does it fill a gap in your routine? Do you like the finish and application method? Can you confirm the shade, ingredients and return policy? If you already own several products that perform the same job, a new colour or format may be more of a novelty than a necessity.

Try new makeup in natural light and build coverage gradually. For skincare products with active ingredients, introduce one new product at a time so it is easier to notice irritation or incompatibility. Check individual brand channels for the latest product details, because shades and availability can vary by market.

Beauty launches can make routines feel fresh, but a thoughtful choice is more useful than buying every new release. Focus on the products you will enjoy using consistently.

Context: BeautyMatter’s beauty industry coverage and Dubai Beauty Spot’s SHEGLAM launch report.

title: AIVI Brings Personalised Shopping Features to Retail in the GCC
excerpt: Apparel Group’s AIVI platform brings together personalised discovery, virtual try-on and shopping features. Here is what these tools can and cannot do for beauty shoppers.
body:
Digital retail is moving beyond a simple product catalogue. Apparel Group’s AIVI platform brings together shopping discovery features such as virtual try-on, an AI-powered fashion assistant, social commerce and a loyalty programme. Although AIVI is a broader shopping platform rather than a beauty-only service, these features reflect how online retail is trying to make browsing more personalised.

What AIVI offers

On its official AIVI page, Apparel Group describes the platform as an evolution of 6thStreet into a wider digital shopping experience. The company has also published a separate announcement about the AIVI launch. Features and delivery options may vary by market and participating brand, so shoppers should check the current app or website for the services available in their location.

How personalisation can help

Recommendations can make a large catalogue easier to navigate and may help shoppers discover products related to their preferences. Virtual try-on tools can also provide a visual reference, but they should not be treated as a guarantee that a shade, fit or finish will look exactly the same in person. Screen settings, lighting and the quality of the product listing all affect what you see.

Beauty shopping still needs a careful check

Before ordering cosmetics or skincare online, read the full product description and ingredient list, confirm the seller, check delivery estimates and review the returns policy. For complexion products, use shade references and swatches as a guide rather than a promise. If a platform asks you to save preferences, share only the information you are comfortable providing and review privacy settings where available.

A personalised interface can make shopping more convenient, but it does not replace informed product selection. Use digital tools to narrow your options, then confirm the details that matter before you buy.

Sources: Apparel Group’s official AIVI page and AIVI launch announcement.

title: A Simple Skincare Routine for Dubai’s Air-Conditioned Days
excerpt: A practical five-step routine for Dubai’s air-conditioned days, from gentle cleansing and moisturising to daily sun protection and knowing when to simplify.
tip1: Start with a gentle cleanse. In the morning, rinse or use a mild cleanser depending on how your skin feels. At night, cleanse thoroughly to remove sunscreen, makeup and daily build-up. If your face feels tight after washing, try a gentler formula or shorter cleansing routine.
tip2: Keep active ingredients simple. If you use exfoliating acids, retinoids or other targeted products, follow their directions and introduce only one new product at a time. Combining several new treatments at once can make it harder to identify what is causing irritation.
tip3: Moisturise for comfort. Air-conditioned rooms can leave some skin feeling dry or tight. Apply a moisturiser suited to your skin while it still feels slightly damp after cleansing. Adjust the texture to your needs rather than adding several layers automatically.
tip4: Make sun protection a daily habit. Use broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher as directed. Reapply according to the label, especially after sweating, swimming or spending extended time outdoors. A moisturiser or foundation with SPF should not automatically replace a dedicated sunscreen unless used as directed in a sufficient amount.
tip5: Let your skin guide adjustments. If irritation persists, simplify your routine and pause recently introduced products. Seek advice from a qualified dermatologist for ongoing discomfort or concerns, rather than repeatedly adding new products.

title: How to Make Your Manicure Last Longer Between Salon Visits
excerpt: Help your manicure stay neat between salon visits with five practical habits for moisturising, protecting your hands and avoiding damage to natural nails.
tip1: Moisturise hands and cuticles daily. Apply hand cream after washing and use cuticle oil when convenient, especially if your hands feel dry. Massage gently around the nail rather than cutting or aggressively pushing back the cuticle.
tip2: Protect your manicure during chores. Wear suitable gloves for dishwashing and cleaning to reduce prolonged water exposure and contact with detergents. Dry your hands well afterwards and moisturise to keep the surrounding skin comfortable.
tip3: Use your fingertips, not your nails, as tools. Opening tins, scraping labels and picking at hard surfaces can stress the free edge and cause chips or breaks. Keep a small tool nearby for everyday tasks instead.
tip4: Never peel lifting gel polish. Picking or pulling product away can remove layers of the natural nail with it. If you notice lifting, avoid catching it on clothing and arrange professional removal or repair rather than covering it with another layer.
tip5: Book maintenance when wear becomes noticeable. Chips, lifting or significant regrowth are signs to arrange a refresh that suits the product and your nails. Do not try to glue down lifted product or continue wearing a damaged enhancement if it catches or feels uncomfortable.

title: A Soft, Fluffy Brow Look in Five Easy Steps
excerpt: Create softly brushed-up brows with a spoolie, light pencil strokes and brow gel. These five steps keep the finish natural rather than overly drawn-on.
tip1: Brush before adding colour. Use a clean spoolie to comb hairs upwards and outwards, following their natural direction. This reveals sparse areas and helps you see the shape before you apply product.
tip2: Fill only where needed. Use a fine pencil or suitable brow product to add short, light strokes that resemble hair. Start with less product than you think you need, especially at the front of the brow.
tip3: Soften the edges. Brush through again with the spoolie to diffuse any strong marks and blend the colour. A soft brow usually looks more natural when the inner edge is lighter than the arch and tail.
tip4: Set hairs with a small amount of brow gel. Brush in the direction you want the hairs to sit and follow the product instructions. Avoid applying too much at once, which can leave visible residue or make hairs feel stiff.
tip5: Check both brows in natural light. Step back from the mirror and compare the overall shape rather than trying to make every hair identical. Add a little more only where it improves balance, then let the product set.

title: Heat-Proof Your Everyday Makeup Without Heavy Layers
excerpt: Keep everyday makeup comfortable in warm Dubai weather with thin layers, suitable long-wear formulas and smart touch-ups that do not replace sunscreen.
tip1: Prepare skin with products that work together. Apply a comfortable moisturiser and broad-spectrum sunscreen, then give each layer time to settle before makeup. If products pill or slide, simplify the layers and test combinations before an important day.
tip2: Use thin, targeted coverage. Apply a small amount of foundation or skin tint and add concealer only where needed. Lighter layers are often easier to refresh than a heavy base, particularly when you are moving between air-conditioned spaces and outdoor heat.
tip3: Choose long-wear products selectively. Consider transfer-resistant formulas on areas where makeup tends to move, such as the sides of the nose or eyelids. You do not need every product to be matte or long-wearing; choose finishes that feel comfortable on your skin.
tip4: Blot before powdering. If shine appears, gently press a clean tissue or blotting paper onto the area first. Then use a small amount of powder only where needed. Layering powder over excess oil can make makeup look heavy or uneven.
tip5: Plan touch-ups and sun protection separately. Carry blotting papers and the makeup products you actually need. Follow your sunscreen’s reapplication instructions during outdoor time; makeup alone does not provide reliable sun protection, and reapplication methods should suit your sunscreen and activities.

title: A Better Hair-Wash Routine for Smooth, Manageable Hair
excerpt: Build a more manageable wash routine by matching shampoo to your scalp, conditioning dry lengths and reducing friction and unnecessary heat.
tip1: Choose shampoo for your scalp. Consider whether your scalp tends to feel oily, dry or sensitive and wash as often as your hair and activity level require. There is no single schedule that suits everyone, so adjust based on comfort and build-up.
tip2: Massage gently with your fingertips. Work shampoo across the scalp without scratching with your nails. Let the lather rinse through the lengths rather than aggressively rubbing the hair together, which can increase tangling and friction.
tip3: Condition the areas that need it. Apply conditioner mainly through the mid-lengths and ends if those parts feel dry or rough. Follow the product directions and rinse thoroughly; fine hair may need a lighter formula or a smaller amount.
tip4: Reduce friction after washing. Gently squeeze out excess water and blot with a soft towel instead of rubbing vigorously. Detangle in sections from the ends upwards using a suitable wide-tooth comb or brush, taking extra care when hair is wet and fragile.
tip5: Style with heat thoughtfully. Use a heat protectant designed for your styling routine and follow its directions. Choose the lowest practical temperature and avoid repeatedly passing hot tools over the same section. If your hair feels increasingly dry or breaks easily, reduce heat and consider professional advice.

title: The Modern Salon Self-Care Ritual: Small Moments That Feel Luxurious
excerpt: A salon visit can be more than a beauty appointment. Plan a little breathing room, choose a service that suits your needs and leave with aftercare you can manage.
body:
Self-care does not have to mean an elaborate schedule or a long list of products. Sometimes it is simply setting aside time for a service you enjoy and giving yourself permission to slow down. A salon appointment can be a small reset in a busy week, especially when you plan it around what you actually need rather than trying to fit everything into one visit.

Choose the appointment that suits your day

Start with one clear priority. You might want a fresh manicure, a hair refresh, tidy brows or time for a treatment you have been considering. Choosing the main service first helps you plan your time and budget, and makes it easier to explain what you would like when you arrive. If you want several services, ask in advance how long the combination is likely to take.

Arrive with a little breathing room

Where possible, leave enough time to arrive without rushing. Bring reference photos if you have a particular colour, shape or finish in mind. Photos are useful for communicating the general direction, but your hair texture, nail length and skin needs may affect the final result. A consultation gives your stylist or therapist a chance to explain what is realistic and suggest alternatives when needed.

Make the experience comfortable

Let the salon team know about relevant preferences, such as how you like your nails shaped, how much length you want removed or whether you prefer a quieter appointment where possible. If you have allergies, sensitivities or a history of reactions to products, mention them before the service begins. Clear communication helps everyone understand your expectations.

Leave with a simple aftercare plan

Before you leave, ask which two or three steps will help you maintain the result at home. This might mean moisturising your hands and cuticles, using heat protection before styling or following the recommended care instructions for a treatment. You do not need to buy a full shelf of products if a few consistent habits are enough.

Make the ritual your own

The most useful salon ritual is one that fits your schedule, preferences and budget. You might book a regular maintenance appointment or simply visit when you want a refresh. Luxury is not about doing more; it is about making a considered choice and enjoying the time you have set aside.

title: How to Choose a Nail Shape That Suits Your Hands and Lifestyle
excerpt: Almond, oval, square and squoval nails each create a different look. Compare the shapes and choose one that works with your natural nails, daily tasks and preferred upkeep.
body:
Nail shape can change the feel of a manicure even when you choose a neutral polish. Some shapes create a tapered, elongated look, while others feel clean, classic or practical at shorter lengths. The best choice is not only about what is trending. It should also suit your natural nail length, the shape of your nail beds, your everyday activities and how much maintenance you are comfortable with.

Almond: tapered and elegant

Almond nails narrow towards a soft point and can give fingers an elongated appearance. They generally need some length to form the taper, so they may not be the easiest option if your natural nails are very short or prone to breaking. If you like this shape, ask your nail technician what length is realistic for your nails and whether an extension would be needed to achieve the look.

Oval: soft and versatile

Oval nails follow a rounded curve at the tip. They can work well on short to medium lengths and are a good option if you want a softer outline without a pointed finish. Because the edges are rounded, the shape can also feel comfortable for people who use their hands frequently.

Square: crisp and structured

Square nails have straight sides and a flatter tip, creating a more defined look. This shape can suit short or medium nails, although the corners may catch more easily depending on length and daily activity. Ask your technician to check that the corners are even and comfortable rather than excessively sharp.

Squoval: a practical middle ground

Squoval combines a square outline with softened corners. It offers a neat, balanced appearance and can be an easy shape to maintain, especially at shorter lengths. If you are unsure which shape to choose, squoval is a useful starting point to discuss at your appointment.

Match the shape to your routine

If you type often, handle equipment or do tasks that put pressure on your nails, a shorter oval or squoval shape may be more practical than a long, tapered style. No shape is unbreakable, and longer nails generally need more care to avoid catching or damage. Choose a length you can comfortably manage between appointments.

Bring a reference, then personalise it

Save a photo that shows the shape you like, but remember that the same shape may look different depending on nail length and natural proportions. Discuss your preferences with your nail technician and ask for a shape that feels comfortable as well as polished. A good manicure should fit your life, not make everyday tasks harder.

title: A Guide to Choosing Hair Treatments Without Overcomplicating Your Routine
excerpt: The right hair treatment depends on your hair’s condition, styling habits and the result you want. Start with a clear goal and ask the right questions before booking.
body:
Hair treatments can be designed for different goals, from improving manageability and softness to supporting colour maintenance or creating a smoother finish. With so many services and product names to choose from, it can be tempting to book the treatment that sounds most popular. A better starting point is to identify what you want to change and discuss whether the service is appropriate for your hair.

Start with your main concern

Think about what you notice day to day. Are your ends feeling dry? Is your hair difficult to detangle, looking dull after colouring or becoming hard to style? Do you want to maintain a colour result or make your routine easier? Describe the concern in simple terms instead of choosing a service by name alone. Your stylist can assess your hair and explain which options may suit your goal.

Share your hair history

Previous colour, bleaching, chemical straightening, heat styling and home treatments can all affect the condition of your hair and which services are suitable. Be open about recent colour changes and any products or treatments you have used. If your hair has become unusually fragile or your scalp is irritated, explain that before proceeding so the stylist can advise you appropriately.

Understand what the treatment can and cannot do

Before booking, ask what the service is intended to improve, how long it takes, whether it involves heat or chemicals and what the result is likely to look like on your hair type. Ask how long the effect may last and what factors can affect it. Be cautious of claims that promise a guaranteed result for every person, because hair condition, maintenance and styling habits vary.

Ask about aftercare and upkeep

A treatment may come with specific washing, styling or product recommendations. Find out whether you need to change your shampoo, avoid certain styling habits or return for maintenance. Consider the time and cost of aftercare before committing, especially if the result requires regular upkeep.

Keep your home routine manageable

Many routines can start with a shampoo suited to your scalp, conditioner for the lengths and ends when needed, gentle detangling and heat protection when using hot tools. Add specialist products only when they address a clear need. More steps do not automatically mean better results, and using too many products can make it harder to understand what works for your hair.

Choose based on your hair, not the trend

The right treatment plan should fit your hair history, desired result, budget and willingness to maintain it. A clear consultation and realistic expectations are more valuable than selecting a service simply because it is popular.

title: From Workday to Evening: A Polished Beauty Look in 10 Minutes
excerpt: Refresh your daytime makeup for evening plans with targeted touch-ups, a little extra definition and a lip colour that is easy to reapply.
body:
If you have plans after work, you do not need to remove all your makeup and start again. A few targeted adjustments can make your look feel more defined while keeping the finish fresh. The key is to refresh what has worn away, choose one feature to emphasise and avoid layering too much product over makeup that has already been on your skin for hours.

Minutes 1–2: refresh the base

Look at your skin in good light before adding anything. Use blotting papers or a clean tissue to lift excess shine, especially around the nose and forehead. If foundation has worn away, add a small amount of concealer or base only where needed and blend the edges. If an area feels dry, avoid piling on powder or foundation; a minimal touch of suitable moisturiser may be more comfortable.

Minutes 3–5: add definition to the eyes

For a quick change, blend a slightly deeper eyeshadow close to the lash line or soften the outer corner with a small brush. Tidy brows with a spoolie and use brow gel if you want extra definition. If you choose to refresh mascara, follow the product directions and avoid repeatedly layering over a coat that has become dry or clumpy. You can also keep the eyes simple and let the lip colour do more of the work.

Minutes 6–7: bring back cheek colour

A little blush can help bring colour back to the face after a long day. Choose a formula that layers well over your existing base and apply a small amount, blending towards the temples. If you already have bronzer or contour in place, add only what is needed rather than rebuilding every step.

Minutes 8–9: choose an evening lip

A lipstick in a deeper shade can make a look feel more evening-ready, while a tinted balm keeps it relaxed and easy to maintain. Remove any uneven lip colour, apply the product carefully and check the edges. If you are wearing a bold shade, take it with you for touch-ups rather than trying to make it last all evening without maintenance.

Minute 10: check the overall balance

Step back from the mirror and check your makeup in natural or neutral light if possible. If the eyes are more defined, you may prefer a softer lip; if you have chosen a strong lip colour, keep the rest of the look balanced. A compact mirror, lip product and blotting papers are often enough for later touch-ups.

Keep the routine flexible

These steps are a guide, not a strict rule. Your skin type, the makeup you already wear and the occasion will affect what you need. The aim is to make a few intentional changes that help you feel polished without carrying your entire makeup bag or starting from scratch.

title: The Beauty Routine That Works: Consistency Over Complexity
excerpt: A useful beauty routine is one you can maintain. Focus on the basics, choose products with a purpose and make changes gradually instead of chasing every trend.
body:
A bathroom shelf full of products does not automatically make a beauty routine more effective. When there are too many steps, it can become difficult to stay consistent or work out which products are helping. A routine is more useful when every step has a purpose and the whole process fits your real schedule, budget and preferences.

Keep the basics steady

For many people, a straightforward skincare routine begins with gentle cleansing, moisturising and daytime sun protection. The right products depend on your skin and individual needs, but you do not need to add several treatments at once to get started. For hair, focus on a shampoo suited to your scalp, conditioner where needed and sensible heat protection when styling. For nails, regular hand and cuticle moisturising and avoiding picking at gel polish can support a neater manicure.

Add a product for a clear reason

Before buying something new, ask what you want it to do. Is it addressing a concern you have, replacing a product that has run out or simply repeating something you already own? If two products serve the same purpose, you may not need both. Reading directions and ingredient lists can help you make a more considered choice.

Introduce changes gradually

Changing several skincare products at the same time can make it harder to identify what caused irritation or what actually suits you. Introduce one new product at a time and follow its directions. If you have sensitive skin, a known allergy or a persistent skin concern, seek advice from a qualified healthcare professional before adding products that may not be suitable.

Make the routine fit your day

If mornings are busy, keep the essential steps within reach and leave optional treatments for another time. You might prepare your hair tools the night before, keep hand cream near your desk or carry the lip colour you use most. Small practical changes can make it easier to repeat the habits you care about.

Review what is working

Every so often, notice which products you actually use, which ones feel comfortable and which steps seem unnecessary. Check expiry dates and storage instructions, and avoid keeping products that repeatedly cause irritation. Simplifying a routine is not a failure; it is a way to make it more personal and manageable.

Consistency is not the same as never changing

Your needs may shift with the season, lifestyle or a change in hair or skin condition. You can adapt your routine thoughtfully without replacing everything whenever a new trend appears. The most useful beauty routine is one that supports your needs and is realistic enough to maintain.
